data.title: Backend Framework
data.tagline: Use a shared structure for routes, requests, data, and server behavior
data.description: A backend framework supplies conventions and tools for routing, input handling, middleware, databases, and responses. It reduces repeated setup, but it does not decide the product's rules for you. Choose one that fits the language, hosting model, and size of the application.

use: Give a team a common project structure
avoid: Adopt a large framework for one tiny function without need
Mix several frameworks in the same service casually
Put business rules inside framework-specific glue everywhere
Assume framework defaults match every security requirement

lessonPractice.title: A project already uses Next.js Route Handlers and now needs a sign-up endpoint. What is the better approach?

options.label: Follow the existing routing, validation, and error patterns, put sign-up logic in the matching handler, and verify success and failure requests
options.feedback: Correct. The framework supplies consistent entry and shared handling; new business logic should follow that structure and be verified with real requests.

options.label: Install Express just for sign-up so two frameworks can maintain separate routes and error formats
options.feedback: Maintaining two routing and error systems increases debugging cost, and this request does not justify a second framework.

options.label: Copy a framework example that always returns success, then add validation and sign-up logic after the page is finished
options.feedback: A fixed success response does not prove an account was created and makes unfinished business logic appear usable.

data.agentPrompt: Inspect the backend framework and directory conventions already used by this project; do not introduce a second framework. Follow the existing pattern to add `POST /api/signup`: accept email and password, validate the input, call the sign-up logic, return the new account on success, and return a clear reason on failure. Then send one valid request and one request without an email, verify the status codes, response bodies, and server logs, and list the files you changed.
